look_here_first: Ignore the flower at first and look underwater: submerged leaves are opposite and fan-shaped, split into many fine segments. When flowering, a small white-to-purplish 3-merous flower rises at the surface.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: rooted submerged perennial with slender branched stems

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: submerged leaf blades fan-shaped and repeatedly dichotomously divided into fine segments

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small floating leaves may appear near flowering shoots

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: solitary axillary flowers at or above the water surface

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers 3-merous: three sepals and three petals

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Rooted perennial submerged aquatic with much-branched slender stems.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Strongly heterophyllous: the common submerged leaves are opposite, fan-shaped and finely divided; small linear floating leaves may be produced near flowering.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Solitary axillary 3-merous flower, generally white to purplish with yellow nectar-bearing auricles.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Small fruits with one to three seeds.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's San Marcos River frame gives a close flower view; combine it with the unmistakable opposite fan-shaped submerged foliage for identification.
